_doc: GenSeo persona bank taxonomy. 200 slots / 50 sourcing cells / 10 rotation pools. Rotation happens at POOL level (gender+age); ethnicity cells are sourcing quotas only, so a cell of 1 never forces a persona repeat.

gaze_values.phrase: eyes looking straight into the lens
eyes just past the lens, as if at someone standing beside the camera
eyes down on the product, reading it
eyes down on their own hands, mid-task
eyes off into the room, mid-thought, not at anything in particular
eyes raised and away from the lens, toward a window or the ceiling
eyes on someone just out of frame, mid-conversation

face_angle_values.phrase: head squared to the lens, both ears equally visible, chin level with the lens
face_angle_values.frame_hint: in the frame: the nose points straight at the lens, both ears show about equally, and the face is centred on the head silhouette — there is no left/right turn at all

face_angle_values.phrase: head squared to the lens, both ears equally visible, chin dipped about 12 degrees below level, brow toward camera
face_angle_values.frame_hint: in the frame: the nose points straight at the lens, both ears show about equally, and the face is centred on the head silhouette — there is no left/right turn at all

face_angle_values.phrase: head squared to the lens, both ears equally visible, chin raised about 10 degrees above level, jawline lengthened
face_angle_values.frame_hint: in the frame: the nose points straight at the lens, both ears show about equally, and the face is centred on the head silhouette — there is no left/right turn at all

face_angle_values.phrase: head turned about 35 degrees to their left, the far cheek narrowing, chin level with the lens
face_angle_values.frame_hint: in the frame this means: the NOSE points toward the RIGHT edge of the image, and the ear nearest the camera is the subject's RIGHT ear, sitting on the LEFT side of the head silhouette. Judge the turn by which EAR you can see, not by which way it feels — 'to their left' is the subject's own left, which is the opposite of the viewer's.

_axes_doc: THREE INDEPENDENT AXES, deliberately non-overlapping so a prompt can carry all three without contradicting itself. face_angle = where the HEAD points (yaw x pitch); this is the axis under Kevin's 2026-08-10 hard rule and it may NEVER repeat for a given persona. gaze = where the EYES point RELATIVE to the head. shot = where the CAMERA is and how much of the scene it takes. The pre-2026-08-10 gaze_values mixed head orientation ('profile', 'over-shoulder') into the eye axis, which is why they had to be rewritten: face_angle cannot be enforced against a vocabulary that already secretly encodes it.
face_angle_rule: HARD RULE (Kevin, 2026-08-10): never generate the same face angle twice for one model. Per persona, every id in face_angle_values may be used at most ONCE, ever - hero and inline count separately. 21 angles per persona x 200 personas = 4200 unique hero images before the bank can repeat anything. Enforced in persona_picker.py (selection refuses a used angle and skips exhausted personas), in article_images.py (--face-angle is mandatory with --persona-ref and is rejected if already used), and in the QC rubric (the vision gate FAILs an image whose head angle does not match the assigned one).
